title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 53–55): Grothendieck is studying 'ateliers' (workshops). These are structures made of 'figures' X carrying a sub-figure relation ⊴ and a support/incidence datum |∘|. The model case is the 'spatial' atelier Atopat(Σ) (called Figspat(Σ) on p. 55) of figures over an 'organisation' Σ. An organisation is a poset (Σ, ≤) with an extra datum C, perhaps a covering or closure relation, presumably with enough sups. Each figure X = (Φ, ρ) has a top element X° ∈ Σ, its 'support'.

On p. 53 he wants to encode a general atelier A by a triple (≤, C, A): an organisation Σ together with a subset A ⊂ Atopat(Σ). On this page he states the axioms on A that are meant to be the only ones needed:
(Atopat 1') A is downward closed in Atopat(Σ) for ⊴: if X ∈ A and Y ⊴ X, then Y ∈ A. This is the analogue of 'Ateliers 1' for set-theoretic ateliers over a base set L.
(Atopat 2') Let Σ' = {X° | X ∈ A} ⊂ Σ. For every S ∈ Σ, S = Sup{ξ ∈ Σ' | ξ ≤ S}. In other words, the supports of figures in A form a join-dense subset of Σ, a 'base' in the locale-theoretic sense. This replaces 'Ateliers 2' (∀x ∈ L, {{x}} ∈ A): the singleton figures generate. A crossed-out first attempt (Atop. 2) used A_S = {X ∈ A | X° ≤ S} and a subset Σ_0; that idea reappears as the map β on p. 55.

Expectation, stated as a conjecture ('Je m'attends que'): with the induced atelier structure, A is a spatial atelier. Moreover there is a canonical isomorphism Σ ≃ Σ_A, where Σ_A is the space reconstructed intrinsically from A. Under it, the canonical map A → Atopat(Σ_A) (the 'Sup' map) corresponds to the inclusion A ⊂ Atopat(Σ).

Page 55 starts the verification. Axioms Atspat 1 and 2 are called trivial. For Atspat 3 he uses the maps α: X ↦ X° and β: S ↦ {X ∈ A | X° ≤ S}, which give mutually inverse bijections. So this is a reconstruction theorem: a spatial atelier is determined by any downward-closed family of figures whose supports form a base of the organisation. It is the analogue, for 'organisations', of recovering a space or locale from a base, or a frame from a join-dense generating subposet.
errors: The main statement is only a conjecture on this page ('Je m'attends que'); the proof is attempted on p. 55.
Atopat 2' assumes the relevant sups exist in Σ, which presumably follows from the axioms on organisations; this is not stated here.

Join-density of Σ' alone cannot recover the poset Σ from Σ' (many lattices contain the same join-dense subposet). The reconstruction Σ ≃ Σ_A must therefore use the extra data of A (supports, ⊴, and probably C). The page does not make explicit why that suffices, and p. 55 only treats the |∘| part.
The axioms are labelled 'the two only (?) conditions'; Grothendieck himself marks with a query whether these two conditions suffice.

ideas.what: Sub-atelier of Atopat(Σ) closed downward under the sub-figure relation ⊴
Condition that the supports X° of figures in A are join-dense in Σ (S = Sup of the elements of Σ' below S)
ideas.modern_name: join-dense subset / base of a locale or frame
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical lattice theory; locale theory (Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone)

ideas.what: Conjectured reconstruction: a downward-closed A ⊂ Atopat(Σ) with join-dense supports is a spatial atelier, with canonical Σ ≃ Σ_A identifying A → Atopat(Σ_A) with the inclusion
ideas.modern_name: reconstruction of a space from a generating family of 'figures' (cf. a space as reconstructed from its basic opens; concrete sites)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct analogue for 'ateliers'; analogous results in locale theory and concrete sheaf/diffeological settings

missed.claim: The 1986 theory of 'ateliers' (spatial vs. set-theoretic ateliers over organisations) contains a characterization/reconstruction theorem for spatial ateliers by two axioms. This axiomatics of figure-based spaces is unpublished and not developed in the literature. The page itself is a routine lattice-theoretic step within it.
missed.quote: Je m'attends que, pour de telles données, la partie en question A de Atopat(Σ), munie de la structure d'atelier induite, est un atelier spatial, et que l'on a un iso. can. Σ ≃ Σ_A
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Ateliers look like a precursor axiomatics of 'spaces defined by their figures', in the spirit of concrete sites, diffeological spaces and spaces of plots. The page could be of interest to historians tracing Grothendieck's late foundational work. The mathematical content of this page alone is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The concrete content is order theory (downward closure plus a join-dense base gives reconstruction), and it is stated as a conjecture. The only mildly notable aspect is that it belongs to the unpublished 1986 'ateliers' framework.
transcription_corrections: 'Atop{+Cat[?]+} 1'' is probably 'Atopat 1'' (the name used for the axioms in parallel with Atopat(Σ)); likewise 'Atop. 2'' should read 'Atopat 2''.
'Atop(Σ)' should read 'Atopat(Σ)' throughout, consistent with the previous page and the last line.
'partie un [?] questions A de Atop(Σ)' should read 'la partie en question A de Atopat(Σ)'.
'définie [?] l'inclusion' is likely 'déduite de l'inclusion' (or similar).
Page numbering: the manuscript page number is 54; 57 is the archive number in the lower margin.
